title: Read profiler reports
brief: Parse a recorded ncu CSV and nsys stats export, place a kernel on the roofline from raw counters, and write a classifier that names a kernel memory-bound, compute-bound, latency-bound, uncoalesced, bank-conflicted, or tail-limited, and a timeline launch-bound or sync-bound. The checks are pure Python and run without a GPU.
hints: parse_ncu_csv: find the line that starts with "ID", pass the lines from there to csv.DictReader, and strip commas from Metric Value before float(). The ==PROF== lines before and after the table are not rows. Key each value by Kernel Name, then Metric Name.

An FFMA is two FLOPs: a multiply and an add. sgemm_tiled counts 68,719,476,736 FFMA, which is 4096 cubed, so its work is 2 x 4096 cubed plus the 4096 squared alpha multiplies. The ridge point is peak FLOP/s over bytes/s: 19.5e12 / 1935e9 is 10.08 FLOP per byte.

Occupancy: the smallest of the four launch__occupancy_limit_* values is the resident blocks per SM. Multiply by warps per block, ceil(block / 32), and divide by 64. reduce_tail holds one block of 8 warps, which is 12.5 percent.

Sector efficiency is useful bytes over 32 x sectors. A strided load that uses 4 bytes of every 32-byte sector scores 0.125. A coalesced float4 load fetches 16 sectors per request and scores 1.0, so a rule on sectors per request alone is wrong.

Bank conflicts: divide the conflict counters by the wavefront counters, and add ld and st before you divide. A 32-way conflict on loads is 31 conflict wavefronts for each 32 wavefronts, a fraction of 0.97.

Waves: grid / (108 x blocks per SM). reduce_tail has 120 blocks and one resident per SM, 1.111 waves, so the second wave runs 12 blocks on 108 SMs. wave_efficiency is 1.111 / 2 = 0.556. A kernel with 303.4 waves loses 0.2 percent.

diagnose runs the structural rules first. transpose_naive_smem sits at 30 percent DRAM and 21 percent SM: a classifier that reads only those two numbers calls it latency-bound. copy_strided is at 62 percent DRAM and looks memory-bound until you count sectors.
busy_and_gaps: sort the (start, start + duration) intervals, merge those that overlap, then sum the merged lengths. Adding the durations makes two overlapped streams look 189 percent busy.

diagnose_timeline: pass only the kernel events to busy_and_gaps. SYNC_BOUND has 12 kernels of 350 microseconds and pauses near 900 microseconds. LAUNCH_BOUND has 3 microsecond kernels 7.5 microseconds apart, against a 5.1 microsecond launch call.

The live check profiles one PyTorch add with ncu. It skips, with a message, when there is no GPU, no ncu, or no permission to read performance counters. The container error for that is ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM.
